rules.title: Final page served over HTTP
rules.plain_english: The site itself is not encrypted. Anything visitors type can be read in transit.
rules.remediation: Install a TLS certificate and serve the site only over HTTPS.

rules.title: Site unreachable or returning an error
rules.plain_english: Visitors cannot load the site. Nothing else matters until this is fixed.
rules.remediation: Confirm DNS, hosting, and TLS certificate. Check origin and CDN status pages. Restore service before any other remediation.

rules.title: HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS
rules.plain_english: Visitors who type the address without https can be intercepted. Force the secure version.
rules.remediation: Configure a permanent (301/308) redirect from http:// to https:// at the CDN or web server.

rules.title: Mixed content on an HTTPS page
rules.plain_english: Some parts of the secure page are loaded insecurely, which browsers block or warn about.
rules.remediation: Change every http:// resource reference to https:// or a protocol-relative path.

rules.title: No SPF record
rules.plain_english: Anyone on the internet can send email that appears to come from your domain.
rules.remediation: Publish a TXT record at the domain apex starting v=spf1, listing every service that sends mail for you, and ending in ~all or -all.

rules.title: SPF does not restrict senders
rules.plain_english: Your domain looks protected but is not. The record permits anyone to send as you.
rules.remediation: End the SPF record in ~all (softfail) or -all (fail). Never +all, which authorises every sender, and not ?all, which declines to say.

rules.title: Multiple SPF records
rules.plain_english: You have two SPF records, so receiving servers ignore both. Your domain is as spoofable as if you published none.
rules.remediation: Merge every v=spf1 record into a single TXT record. Combine the include: mechanisms rather than publishing one record per provider.

rules.title: No DMARC record
rules.plain_english: Nothing tells receiving servers what to do with forged mail from your domain, so they deliver it.
rules.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _dmarc.<domain> starting v=DMARC1. Begin with p=none and a rua= address, read the reports, then move to quarantine and reject.

rules.title: Multiple DMARC records
rules.plain_english: You have two DMARC records, so receiving servers ignore both and treat your domain as having no policy. This is worse than the single weak record you replaced.
rules.remediation: Delete every DMARC record at the name except the one you intend to publish. This is usually the result of adding a new record instead of editing the existing one; edit in place next time.

rules.title: Missing Strict-Transport-Security header
rules.plain_english: Browsers are not told to always use the secure connection. One header fixes it.
rules.remediation: Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains after confirming every subdomain serves HTTPS.

rules.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy
rules.plain_english: There is no policy limiting which scripts can run on the page. This is the main defense against injected code.
rules.remediation: Publish a CSP. Start in report-only mode, then enforce script-src and object-src restrictions.

rules.title: Clickjacking protection missing
rules.plain_english: Another site could load your pages inside a hidden frame to trick visitors into clicking.
rules.remediation: Add Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN.

rules.title: Cookie set without protective flags
rules.plain_english: Login cookies could be read or replayed by scripts or other sites.
rules.remediation: Set Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (or Strict) on session and auth cookies.

rules.title: DMARC is not enforcing
rules.plain_english: Your DMARC record watches impersonation but does not stop it. Forged mail is still delivered.
rules.remediation: Once aggregate reports show only legitimate senders failing, move p=none to p=quarantine, then to p=reject.

rules.title: Slow first response
rules.plain_english: The site is slow to start loading. Slow sites lose visitors and rank lower in search.
rules.remediation: Enable caching or a CDN, reduce server-side work on the homepage, and check hosting capacity.

rules.title: Page language not declared
rules.plain_english: Screen readers do not know which language to use, so pronunciation is wrong.
rules.remediation: Add lang="en" (or the correct language code) to the html element.

rules.title: Page title missing or empty
rules.plain_english: The browser tab and screen readers have no name for this page.
rules.remediation: Add a descriptive title element that names the page and the site.

rules.title: Images missing alternative text
rules.plain_english: People using screen readers cannot tell what these images show.
rules.remediation: Add alt text describing each meaningful image. Use alt="" for purely decorative images.

rules.title: Pinch zoom disabled
rules.plain_english: Visitors with low vision cannot zoom the page on their phone.
rules.remediation: Remove user-scalable=no and any maximum-scale below 2 from the viewport meta tag.

rules.title: Form fields without an accessible label
rules.plain_english: Screen reader users cannot tell what to type into these fields.
rules.remediation: Pair each field with a label element (for/id) or add aria-label.

rules.title: Links with no discernible text
rules.plain_english: Some links are announced as just "link" with no idea where they go.
rules.remediation: Add visible text or aria-label to each link so its purpose is announced.

rules.title: No privacy policy link found
rules.plain_english: Visitors cannot find how their data is used. Most privacy laws require this link.
rules.remediation: Add a visible footer link to a current privacy policy on every page.

rules.title: Form submits to an insecure or external endpoint
rules.plain_english: Information typed into a form may travel unencrypted or to a vendor visitors do not know about.
rules.remediation: Post forms over HTTPS and document any third-party form processor in the privacy policy.

rules.title: Weak HSTS max-age
rules.plain_english: The secure-connection instruction expires too quickly.
rules.remediation: Raise max-age to at least 15552000 seconds (180 days), ideally 31536000.

rules.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options
rules.plain_english: Browsers may guess file types, which can turn harmless files into executable code.
rules.remediation: Add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

rules.title: Missing Referrer-Policy
rules.plain_english: Full page addresses may leak to other sites when visitors click outbound links.
rules.remediation: Add Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

rules.title: Missing Permissions-Policy
rules.plain_english: Browser features like camera and location are not explicitly restricted.
rules.remediation: Add Permissions-Policy disabling camera, microphone, geolocation, and payment unless used.

rules.title: Server software version disclosed
rules.plain_english: The site advertises what software it runs, which helps attackers pick exploits.
rules.remediation: Remove or genericize Server and X-Powered-By headers at the web server or CDN.

rules.title: No security.txt disclosure policy
rules.plain_english: Researchers who find a vulnerability have no published way to report it to you.
rules.remediation: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with Contact and Expires fields per RFC 9116.

rules.title: DMARC has no reporting address
rules.plain_english: Nobody is receiving the reports that would show who is sending mail as your domain.
rules.remediation: Add rua=mailto:<address> to the DMARC record so aggregate reports arrive somewhere a person or a tool reads them.

rules.title: No top-level heading
rules.plain_english: The page has no main heading, which makes it harder to navigate by assistive technology.
rules.remediation: Add a single h1 that describes the page.

rules.title: robots.txt missing
rules.plain_english: Search engines and AI crawlers have no instructions for this site.
rules.remediation: Publish a robots.txt that allows desired crawlers and points to the sitemap.

rules.title: XML sitemap not found
rules.plain_english: Search engines have no map of the site, so pages may be missed.
rules.remediation: Generate an XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt.

rules.title: Third-party trackers loaded before consent could be verified
rules.plain_english: The site uses tracking tools. Depending on where visitors live, consent may be required first.
rules.remediation: Confirm a consent mechanism gates these scripts where required, and list them in the privacy policy.
rules.frameworks: GDPR Art. 6, Art. 7, ePrivacy, CCPA opt-out

rules.title: Meta description missing
rules.plain_english: Search and AI summaries have no short description to show for the site.
rules.remediation: Add a meta description of 120 to 160 characters that states what the site does.

rules.title: AI crawler directives
rules.plain_english: Whether AI assistants may read this site is a policy choice. This lists which crawlers your robots.txt names and which it blocks, so the decision is visible and deliberate rather than accidental.
rules.remediation: Decide which AI crawlers to allow, then record that decision explicitly in robots.txt. Silence is also a decision, but not a recorded one.

rules.title: Canonical link missing
rules.plain_english: Search engines may index duplicate versions of the same page.
rules.remediation: Add a canonical link element pointing to the preferred URL of the page.

rules.title: External script inventory
rules.plain_english: These are the outside companies whose code runs on your site. Keep the list short and known.
rules.remediation: Review each host, remove unused scripts, and add Subresource Integrity where supported.
